note: Every contract edit the requirement walk found and did not make immediately. A finding with no route into an artefact is a finding that gets lost — `handoff/requirement-count.md` named the 22.3 collision on 18 August, said it was worth raising, and it never became a CF. This file is that route. It is hand-authored during the walk and checked by `tools/check-backlog.py`.

lanes.settled: One contract, and that contract already shows how it should look. Fixed at section close; the package stays green.
lanes.deferred: Crosses contracts, or has no precedent to copy. Held until the section named in `blockedOn` is walked, because deciding it now would design it in the wrong contract.
lanes.decision: Needs a client or commercial answer. Belongs in the conflict register, not here — recorded only so the walk can show where it went.

discriminator: Does this edit touch only the contract being walked, and does that contract already contain a precedent for how it should look? Both yes is `settled`. Anything else is `deferred`. The test is applied rather than judged, because judgement produced the wrong answer on BL-002 — a footer looks like an obvious mirror of the header until you notice a header is chrome and a footer is a link surface.

entries.what: `PromoBlock` has `listPromoBlocks` and `createPromoBlock` and no update or delete.
entries.why: The schema carries `state`, `startsAt`, `endsAt` and `sortOrder` — every field that implies amendment — and a tenant can create a promotional block and never change or remove it. `Banner` is the same shape one path up with full CRUD, so the precedent is in the same file.
entries.fix: Add `updatePromoBlock` (PATCH /tenant-config/promo-blocks/{promoBlockId}) and `deletePromoBlock` (DELETE), mirroring `updateBanner` and `deleteBanner` including their permissions and idempotency treatment.
entries.closedBy: updatePromoBlock and deletePromoBlock added to white-label; lineage entries written; 778 operations

entries.what: Footer configuration does not exist. `setHeader` and `HeaderConfig` are present; the string "footer" appears nowhere in the contract.
entries.why: This reads as a mirror of the header and is not one. A header is chrome — layout, logo, menu, colour. A footer is a link surface, and on a guest storefront it carries the legal links, which exist here as `Policy` records with nowhere to surface. `CMS-007 Page Builder` and `CMS-008 Content Blocks` may already own link composition, and building a second link model beside them is how two vocabularies for one thing start.
entries.fix: Decide whether the footer is a `FooterConfig` in its own right or a composition of existing link and content primitives, then build it.
entries.blockedNote: the CMS sections — P13 screens are specified but the requirement rows behind them are not yet walked
entries.closedBy: FooterConfig and setFooter. **A header is chrome and a footer is a link surface** — legal links are held separately from the free-form columns, so a tenant reorganising their footer cannot remove the privacy notice by accident.

entries.what: Tenant-specific notifications have no contract. `marketing-crm` has `listMessageTemplates` and `createMessageTemplate`; nothing joins a template to tenant branding, and `FeatureToggle.pushNotifications` is on or off rather than content.
entries.why: The gap is real and the home is not obvious. Current reading is that this belongs in `marketing-crm` as a tenant-branding reference resolved on the template at send time, rather than as a new white-label operation — but that is a guess until `marketing-crm` is walked.
entries.fix: Resolve sender identity, logo and colour on a message template at send time, in whichever contract owns templates after domain 22 is walked.
entries.blockedNote: 22.x — Marketing & CRM
entries.closedBy: TenantConfig.notificationBranding, resolved on the template at send time. **An operational alert arriving from noreply@ticvai.com is one a guest marks as spam.**

entries.what: Tenant-specific payment methods are partially served. `FeatureToggle` carries `applePay`, `googlePay`, `appleWallet`, `cashOnDelivery` and `guestCheckout`, which are app capabilities. Which acquirer or provider a tenant settles through is configured nowhere.
entries.why: A wallet toggle and an acquirer configuration are different things sharing a phrase. `finance` already owns settlement ingestion and `LegalEntity`, so provider configuration probably belongs beside them — deciding it inside `white-label` would put an acquirer credential in a branding contract.
entries.fix: Model tenant payment-provider configuration in the contract that owns settlement.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. 5.x walked — no tenant payment-provider configuration appeared, and CF-131 now owns the gateway question.
entries.closedBy: TenantConfig.enabledPaymentMethods, resolved against PaymentProvider.supportedMethods. **A tenant enabling a method their provider does not support should fail here rather than at checkout.**

entries.what: Page enablement is not separable from page publication. `ContentPage.status` uses `ContentStatus`, which governs draft and published state; `isReferenced` reports whether anything links to the page.
entries.why: 19.1.13 and 19.1.14 are stated as a pair — modules and pages — and modules got a dedicated `setModuleEnablement` with `isLicensed` and `referencedBy` while pages did not. Whether a tenant needs to disable a published page without unpublishing it is a product question, and `ModuleEnablement` is only a precedent if the answer is yes.
entries.fix: Confirm whether enablement and publication are distinct for pages; if so, mirror `ModuleEnablement`.
entries.blockedNote: the CMS sections
entries.closedBy: ContentPage.isEnabled. **Enablement is not publication** — unpublishing loses the version and disabling does not, so a venue turning off its water-park section for winter does not republish it every spring.

entries.what: Self-service white-label configuration. P13 Venue CMS exists with 20 screens.
entries.why: CF-114 is open on exactly this — the builder is drawn tenant-facing in the storyboards and specified platform-facing. `self-service` is the word under dispute, and it is a commercial question about who operates the CMS rather than a design one. **Unblocked 18 August** — held on CF-114, now closed. **A blocker that outlives its conflict is the backlog decaying in the way this apparatus exists to prevent**, and this is the second time in one day it happened.
entries.closedBy: Resolved by CF-114. **The word under dispute was self-service** — the builder is tenant-facing, and CF-112 puts the branded waiting room and maintenance page into white-label mode alongside it.

entries.what: `layerMapping` declares each role as a single string and cannot express the client's plan.
entries.why: Two layers are both named `Layer 1`, steps arrive on `steps` and `VC-Steps`, and `0` is the AutoCAD default. A name cannot identify a layer in this file.
entries.fix: Make each `layerMapping` role an array of layer references, and key on layer index with the name as a label.
entries.blockedNote: Settled. The seat-map importer is its own precedent and CF-122 records the reasoning.
entries.closedBy: layerMapping roles take arrays (CF-122, closed this morning). **The client file carries two distinct layers both named Layer 1**, steps on two layers, and AutoCAD default 0 — a single string kept one and dropped the rest silently. **Entry left open after the work; closed on the Track 3 sweep.**

entries.what: Section codes carrying Arabic-Indic digits never join to the manifest.
entries.why: The sample plan labels a section with U+06F2. It renders as B2 and is not B2, so `joinOn: sectionAndRow` reports every seat as `unmatchedGeometry` for a reason no operator could diagnose.
entries.fix: State digit and whitespace normalisation on both sides of the join, covering Arabic-Indic and Extended Arabic-Indic ranges.
entries.blockedNote: Settled. The seat-map importer is its own precedent and CF-122 records the reasoning.
entries.closedBy: digitNormalisation, default true (CF-122). **A١ and A1 are one section to a person and two to a comparison**, and the failure is silent — the row simply does not match.

entries.what: Layer names are UTF-16BE PDF strings and decode to mojibake if read naively.
entries.why: The failure is silent — layers are found, they are garbage, and `layerMapping` matches nothing.
entries.fix: Note the encoding on `layerMapping` so the importer decodes before matching.
entries.blockedNote: Settled. The seat-map importer is its own precedent and CF-122 records the reasoning.
entries.closedBy: Layer names decoded before matching (CF-122). **PDF strings arrive UTF-16BE and read as mojibake taken as bytes**, so a role that looks unmatched may simply be undecoded.

entries.what: Repeated manifest imports into one seat map have undefined append-or-replace semantics.
entries.why: Manifests arrive one section per sheet — the sample covers A1–A4 while the plan shows A1–A4, B1–B3 and C1–C3. An operator importing Section B and losing Section A finds out after committing. Whether a partial manifest tops up or supersedes is a design decision, not a wording fix.
entries.fix: Declare the semantics on `importSeatManifest` and surface it in the preview before commit.
entries.blockedNote: 21.x — Seat Management, where the seat-map lifecycle is walked
entries.closedBy: Repeated manifest imports: ImportJob.outcome now distinguishes noSeatsFound from noLayersMatched, and layersFound lists every decoded layer (CF-122).

entries.what: No venue wayfinding map — no point of interest, coordinate or route in any contract.
entries.why: Three places already depend on it: the AI guest capability scope lists `wayfinding`, `maintenance` says a ride out of service is marked on the venue map, and `GST-021 Interactive Map` is specified with `listProducts` and `getWaitTimes`. Whether this is built, taken from a vendor, or dropped is scope. **Unblocked 18 August** — held on CF-123, now closed. **A blocker that outlives its conflict is the backlog decaying in the way this apparatus exists to prevent**, and this is the second time in one day it happened.
entries.closedBy: The venue-map contract (CF-123) — VenuePoint, VenuePath, the navigation graph and one-click publish. **Three places already depended on it**: the AI guest capability scope lists wayfinding, maintenance marks an out-of-service ride on the venue map, and GST-021 existed with nothing behind it.

entries.what: A guest cannot update their own profile.
entries.why: getGuestProfile is audience [staff, guest]; updateGuestProfile is [staff] with GUEST_MANAGE. The three screens calling it are P06 Staff App, P08 Back Office and P13 CMS, so to correct a phone number a guest must ask a staff member. CF-96 fixed this class for 28 guest screens and the underlying pattern was never swept.
entries.blockedNote: 22.x — Marketing & CRM
entries.closedBy: updateMyProfile, guest-callable, with a narrower field set than the staff operation. **CF-96 fixed this class for 28 guest screens and the pattern was never swept.**

entries.what: No portfolio, household or family structure anywhere.
entries.why: **Ten appearances across ten sections and every domain walked.** Section 5.5 specifies it in full — multiple portfolios per account, a primary holder assigning entitlements, transfer between linked portfolios, shared wallets with individual tracking, merging while preserving balances, and restrictions on transfer, spending and age. The platform models a guest as `subjectId` throughout, which is a good decision that does not reach this: `guestLinkId` links a guest across cells and is not a family, and `Wallet.subjectId` is one guest so a shared balance has no owner. Now CF-132.
entries.blockedNote: 5.5 — Portfolio & Entitlement Management
entries.closedBy: Grant extended with subjectId, overSubjectId, overObjectRef, delegationKind, quota and isRevocableBySubject. **A portfolio is delegated authority, not a household table** — primary holder, group leader, corporate enrolment and shared wallet are four requirements the matrix raises separately and one mechanism. **It inherits the audit**, which a bespoke family structure would have needed built. **This does not make the work smaller, it makes it one piece rather than four.**

entries.what: Ticket sharing is not contracted; only transfer is.
entries.why: Transfer moves ownership, sharing does not. GST-045 is named Ticket Delivery & Sharing and calls transferOrderTickets alone. CF-92 records group sharing by in-app QR as raised by Chinmay and confirmed by Qossai on 10 August — minuted, never contracted.
entries.blockedNote: 2.x — Ticketing Sales
entries.closedBy: shareEntitlement. **Transfer changes the holder; a share lets a second person present the same entitlement while the first still owns it.** The owner can revoke and the recipient cannot transfer on — **that asymmetry is the whole point, because a shared family pass should not become a resale chain.** canShareMedia already existed with nothing behind it.

entries.what: Fast track and priority access do not exist anywhere.
entries.why: No fast track, express pass, skip-the-line or priority access in 778 operations — not an enum value, not a description, not a screen. Whether it is a product kind, a queue class or an entitlement attribute is undecided; queue already has priority queueing for VIP and pass holders.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. 5.6 walked — the queue models fastPassAllocationPercent and no fast-track product; fast track exists nowhere.
entries.closedBy: EntitlementTemplate.fastTrackTier. **Fast track existed nowhere** — not an enum value, not a description, not a screen. **An attribute of the entitlement rather than a queue class**, because one ride serves standby and fast-track from one capacity and queue.isFastPass needed something to read.

entries.what: A guest cannot see their membership, its benefits or its history.
entries.why: membership is a ProductKind so purchase and renewal ride the order path, but nothing returns a guest's active memberships with entitlements, nothing surfaces the tier benefits 5.4.31 requires, and nothing shows prior terms or lapses.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. 2.14 confirmed it — membership entitlements exist and no guest-facing view of benefits or history does.
entries.closedBy: getMyMemberships returns active and lapsed with resolved tier benefits. **Lapsed included because a guest deciding whether to renew is comparing against what they had.**

entries.what: A guest is not notified when their turn approaches.
entries.why: The contract notifies on queue closure — 'closing without notifying is not offered' — and 5.6.6A requires notifying a guest by SMS, email, WhatsApp or push when it is nearly their turn. That is the notification the feature exists for.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. 5.6.6 restated it — the queue notifies on closure only, and never when a turn approaches.
entries.closedBy: Queue.notifyBeforeCallMinutes. **A virtual queue with no notification is worse than a physical one** — at least a line is visible.

entries.what: A guest can see loyalty points and cannot spend them, and there is no rewards catalogue.
entries.why: adjustLoyaltyPoints is audience [staff] with LEDGER_POST. GST-036 Loyalty & Rewards calls two read-only operations. games.redeemPrize is arcade credit, a different currency. 22.6 Gamification & Loyalty is the section that decides the model.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. 22.6 confirmed — loyalty currencies exist and no redemption or rewards catalogue does. Clusters with BL-063 and BL-173.
entries.closedBy: redeemLoyaltyPoints, holding through authoriseStoredValue rather than deducting. **Points that accrue and never redeem are a liability with no exit.**

entries.what: A guest can browse and reserve merchandise but cannot buy it.
entries.why: createRetailSale is a till operation. Retail's seven guest-callable operations stop at reserveMerchandise. Whether guest retail purchase goes through the orders cart or a retail-side guest checkout is undecided.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. 4.4 confirmed guest merchandise purchase — listMerchandise and reserveMerchandise are guest-callable, createRetailSale is not.
entries.closedBy: KSK-017 offers reserve-for-collection and says so. **Reserve is not buy** — createRetailSale is a till operation, and the screen is honest about which rather than implying a checkout that does not exist.

entries.what: No guest emergency broadcast.
entries.why: workforce.publishAnnouncement carries an emergency kind with offline-queued acknowledgement and EMP-047 behind it, and it is staff-facing. A venue-wide guest evacuation notice is not a marketing message and has no path.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. 22.9.15 restated operational alerts and 22.9.4 restated event-based notifications — both CF-134.
entries.closedBy: workforce.broadcastToGuests. **A venue-wide evacuation notice is not a marketing message** and must not ride the marketing path — consent and suppression do not apply to a fire. Bypasses quiet hours, throttling and channel preference, which is why it is a separate operation rather than a campaign with a flag. **Two principals for an evacuation**: a venue-wide alarm sent in error empties a park and is not recallable.

entries.what: Lost and found rides generic case management with no item model.
entries.why: Screens exist on P01, P06 and P08, and lostAndFound is a ModuleKey. There is no lost item, no claim, and no match between the two — which is the whole capability.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. 22.3 walked; lost-and-found still rides generic case management with no item, claim or match model.
entries.closedBy: LostItem with foundOrLost, LostItemMatch and getLostItemMatches. **Generic case management holds a conversation about a lost bag and cannot tell you the bag handed in on Tuesday is the one asked about on Monday** — that match is the only thing the module is for. One entity, two directions, because modelling them separately means matching across two tables that drift. **Scored, never auto-claimed**: returning the wrong phone to the wrong person is worse than returning none.

entries.what: No gamification, badges or challenges.
entries.why: gamification is a ModuleKey and nothing else in 778 operations — a tenant can switch on a module that does not exist. 22.6 is named Gamification & Loyalty and is where the model should land if it lands anywhere.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. 22.6 restated gamification in full — now BL-173 and CF-137.
entries.closedBy: Challenge and ChallengeProgress. **Checked against the matrix on 18 August as Chinmay asked** — section 22.6 is twenty requirements and 19.2.73–75 three more, so it is asked for explicitly. **Gamification is not loyalty**: loyalty pays for spend, a challenge pays for behaviour spend does not produce — a second visit, a quiet Tuesday, a ride nobody rides. **A challenge that only rewards spending is a loyalty programme with worse arithmetic.** scope covers family and group challenges and **needs the portfolio work (CF-132) to be more than a label.**

entries.what: Nothing helps a guest find their vehicle.
entries.why: ParkingEntitlement carries plateNumber, plateCountry and facilityId, and no bay, level or space. A locator needs a position the platform never captures.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. 3.4 confirmed no vehicle locator — ParkingEntitlement carries plateNumber and plateCountry and no bay or level.
entries.closedBy: AccessPoint.vehicleLocationCapture. Level and zone captured against the visit so the app can answer it — **the guest who cannot find their car at 11pm is the last impression of the day.**

entries.what: Guest parking payment contradicts a decision already taken.
entries.why: access.yaml scopes pay-per-hour parking out to the parking system's own POS, decided 14 August. 19.2.78 requires parking payments in the guest app. One of the two is wrong and it is a commercial question. **Unblocked 18 August** — it was held on CF-124, which closed. A blocker that outlives its conflict is the backlog decaying in the way this apparatus exists to prevent.
entries.closedBy: Closed by CF-124 — the client decided on 14 August that pay-per-hour parking runs on the parking system POS, and ParkingFacility.takesPayment records it as a read-only false. **19.2.78 is out of scope as written.**

entries.what: No weekday pattern on an entitlement.
entries.why: Camp tickets need access on X days of the week for Y weeks, and 1.1.82 requires weekday-based validity. validityKind has six values and none carries a day pattern. daysOfWeek already exists on fnb.MenuAvailability and promotions.PromotionConditions, so the shape is settled elsewhere in the package.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. 1.3 is closed and weekday patterns on an entitlement did not resolve there.
entries.closedBy: `EntitlementTemplate.daysOfWeek`, using the shape already on `fnb.MenuAvailability` and `promotions.PromotionConditions`. Null means every day, which is what every existing entitlement means today.

entries.what: No calendar-anchored or computed expiry.
entries.why: End-of-month, end-of-year and dynamic expiry. A pass bought on the 20th expiring on the 31st cannot be expressed by validFromOffsetDays plus validForDays. Verified absent with find-capability.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. 1.4 is closed and calendar-anchored expiry did not resolve there.
entries.closedBy: `expiryAnchor` with six values and `expiryDate`. `offsetDays` stays the default so nothing existing changes. **`seasonEnd` anchors to the venue season rather than the calendar.**

entries.what: No purchase eligibility rules.
entries.why: Age, height, residency, nationality, loyalty status, customer profile and geography. admissionProfileId governs where an entitlement admits, not who may buy it. promotions.evaluatePromotions gates a discount, not a sale.
entries.blockedNote: Purchase eligibility rules. Fifth appearance — 1.1, 1.3, 1.6, 2.1. Ready to work; hold for reconciliation clustering.
entries.closedBy: EntitlementTemplate.purchaseEligibility — age, height, residency, nationality, loyalty tier, with requiresVerification. **Evaluated at add-to-cart, not checkout**: a guest told at payment they cannot buy a resident rate has already entered a card.

entries.what: No group product, group leader or attendee model.
entries.why: BO-026 Group Bookings runs on generic order operations, and WEB-011 is named Guest Details & Attendee Forms while calling wishlist, consent and device operations. No group size, quota, group pricing, leader, or per-attendee field capture exists.
entries.blockedNote: 2.x — Ticketing Sales
entries.closedBy: GroupBooking with a leader, expected and confirmed size, minimum, and attendee capture. **The leader is the point** — a school booking forty places has one person who pays, one called if the coach is late, and forty who need names collecting, and a generic order has one guest. **minimumSize means answering the pricing question at booking rather than at the gate.**

entries.what: No Apple or Google Wallet pass mechanism.
entries.why: appleWallet and googlePay are FeatureToggle keys, buildTime on native apps. There is no pass generation, no pass update push, no serial and no authentication token anywhere. In-app and TAIS wallet storage is contracted; the two platform wallets are a switch with nothing behind it.
entries.blockedNote: 19.x, with the guest app surfaces
entries.closedBy: WalletPass with serial, authentication token and push. **A wallet pass is a live object, not a download** — its value over a PDF is that it updates. **A pass that cannot be pushed to is a screenshot with better rounding**, and a gate change reaching one of two registered devices is worse than reaching neither, because the guest will trust the stale one.

entries.what: No product versioning, history or clone.
entries.why: copyPriceList and cloneSeatMap are the precedents and the product equivalent does not exist. ProductVariant is never deleted because orders reference it, which is version discipline without a version record.
entries.blockedNote: Ready, and clusters with BL-047 and BL-058 as one versioned-entity mechanism.
entries.closedBy: `cloneProduct`, following `copyPriceList` and `cloneSeatMap`. **Variants come with it; orders do not** — a clone has no history, which is what makes it a clone rather than a version.

entries.what: No conversion to a term product, and no recurring guest billing.
entries.why: Converting a ticket into a membership or season pass is not a line exchange — the price treatment differs. And nothing bills a guest on a cycle; subscription serves tenant licensing.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. 2.14 confirmed conversion to a term product is unmodelled and recurring guest billing is CF-129.
entries.closedBy: convertToTermProduct. **Not a line exchange, because the price treatment differs** — a conversion credits what the guest paid today against a term product and starts a new validity. **The gate offer that today comes off an annual pass is the most effective upsell a venue has**, and it needed an operation.

entries.what: suspendEntitlement has no inverse.
entries.why: A suspended membership cannot be reactivated. retail.suspendWallet and reinstateWallet are the precedent for a pair in the same package.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. suspendEntitlement still has no inverse after 1.4.
entries.closedBy: `reinstateEntitlement`, following `retail.suspendWallet` / `reinstateWallet`. **Validity is not extended** — the time lost is part of the sanction.

entries.what: A ticket cannot carry stored value, and a gate cannot deduct it.
entries.why: Wallet is bound to subjectId and GiftCard to a cardCode; an entitlement carrying a balance is neither. validateAccess never touches a wallet, so admission-based deduction has no path.
entries.blockedNote: 6.x — Retail POS
entries.closedBy: EntitlementTemplate.carriesStoredValue and includedValue. **The value is a retail.Wallet bound to the entitlement, not a balance on the ticket** — one balance mechanism (CF-126), so it holds authorisations and expires by credit type. A second balance would have been the seventh implementation.

entries.what: No referral model.
entries.why: Referral benefit entitlement. No referrer attribution, no referral reward, nothing anywhere.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. 22.6.10 restated referral challenges; no referral model exists.
entries.closedBy: Referral with a qualifying action. **The reward fires on the referee act, not the sign-up** — a referral paying on registration pays for accounts rather than guests.

entries.what: No corporate account allocations or member enrolment.
entries.why: PartnerAgreement covers commercial terms — net rates, commission, credit. Corporate ticket allocations, quotas and enrolling members under a corporate account are not modelled.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. 2.4 closed without corporate allocations appearing.
entries.closedBy: PartnerAgreement.corporateAllocations. **A corporate account with fifty places for its staff is the same structure as a reseller with fifty to sell** — the difference is that a corporate member does not pay.

entries.what: Time-range and calendar validity live on performances rather than on the entitlement.
entries.why: A time-window entitlement — valid 09:00 to 13:00 on any day — needs a performance to express it today, and there is no blackout or calendar exception on an entitlement. Whether that is correct or a missing dimension on validityKind depends on how 1.3 Event Management uses performances.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. Time-range validity still sits on performances rather than the entitlement.
entries.closedBy: EntitlementTemplate.validTimeWindows and blackoutDates. **A window is a property of the entitlement and a performance is an occurrence** — conflating them means a morning pass generates 365 performances a year.

entries.what: Membership-based eligibility gates a discount, not a purchase.
entries.why: promotions.evaluatePromotions can require membership for a price. Nothing prevents a non-member buying a member-only product. Part of the same question as BL-027 and separated because the mechanism already half exists.
entries.blockedNote: Ready, and now four appearances — 1.1, 2.1.20, 4.1.23, 4.4.26. A membership tier conditions a discount through `PromotionConditions.membershipTierIds`; what is absent is a membership granting entitlements and access rights automatically rather than a price cut.
entries.closedBy: PromotionConditions.purchaseGate. **evaluatePromotions gated a price and nothing gated a sale** — a non-member could buy a member-only product, with only the member price refused. Evaluated at add-to-cart, because a guest told at payment has already entered a card.

entries.what: Donation tax treatment is unstated and separate taxation is required.
entries.why: Donations post to a liability account rather than revenue, which is contracted. 1.1.134 additionally requires separate taxation handling, and whether a donation attracts VAT is a tax question already open as CF-84. **Unblocked 18 August** — held on CF-84, now closed. **A blocker that outlives its conflict is the backlog decaying in the way this apparatus exists to prevent**, and this is the second time in one day it happened.
entries.blockedNote: CF-84
entries.closedBy: TaxCode.appliesTo now carries  (CF-84). **0% is a valid rate, not an absence of one**, and treatment is set per jurisdiction rather than assumed in the posting. The liability-account default stands.

entries.what: No resource entity — no type, category, parent-child relationship or configurable attribute.
entries.why: A cabana is currently a product with an availability envelope, which sells a slot and cannot express a specific object checked out to a guest and returned. Ten requirements define the entity directly and the utilisation reporting behind it has no source.
entries.closedBy: The resources contract — Resource with kind, parent, attributes, setup and teardown. **A venue with forty identical strollers has forty resources**, because guest twelve returned stroller twelve.

entries.what: No resource calendar, conflict detection, recurring reservation, setup and teardown window, or resource package.
entries.why: Depends on the entity in BL-039. Conflict detection before assignment is the whole point of a resource calendar and nothing in the package computes it.
entries.closedBy: getResourceAvailability returns free windows with setup and teardown already subtracted, and bookResource refuses on conflict across every occurrence of a recurrence. **Booking eight of twelve failing after seven succeeded is worse than the whole thing refusing.**

entries.what: No rental check-out and check-in, no deposit taken against a resource, no resource held by a named guest for a period.
entries.why: `shift.DepositBox` is a cash bag allocated to a cashier and unrelated. Rental stock may belong in `inventory` rather than beside the resource entity, which is exactly the kind of home question reconciliation settles.
entries.blockedNote: Ready, and 7.6 states it most completely of anywhere in the matrix — rental products with serial numbers, availability by location, duration and slot pricing, deposits, check-out and check-in with condition capture, late fees, and maintenance windows. 7.6.15 says outright that it is not covered.
entries.closedBy: checkOutResource and checkInResource, with the deposit held through authoriseStoredValue. **A deposit taken and refunded is two transactions and a fee; held and released is neither.** Damage routes the resource to maintenance directly, because routing through available leaves a window where the next guest books a broken item.

entries.what: No staff skill profile, no certification with expiry, no qualification validated before assignment, no dynamic or priority-based allocation.
entries.why: `RotaAssignment` carries `requiredRoleId` alone. A role is not a skill, and 1.2.36 requires the qualification checked *before* the assignment is made — a lifeguard certificate that lapsed is a safety matter, not a reporting one.
entries.closedBy: setResourceQualifications with expiry. **A role is not a skill**, and 1.2.36 requires the check before assignment — a lifeguard certificate that lapsed last month is a safety failure, not a data-quality one.

entries.what: Assets cannot be allocated to an event or activity, and have no depreciation schedule or retirement transition.
entries.why: `maintenance` has the asset, its status, inspections and out-of-service blocking — the foundation is right. Allocation depends on the resource calendar in BL-040, and depreciation may be a `finance` concern rather than a maintenance one. **Unblocked 18 August** — held on CF-125, now closed. **A blocker that outlives its conflict is the backlog decaying in the way this apparatus exists to prevent**, and this is the second time in one day it happened.
entries.fix: Extend the asset with allocation and lifecycle once the resource model is decided.
entries.blockedNote: CF-125, and 5.x accounting for depreciation
entries.closedBy: Asset.resourceId, depreciation and retirement. **An AV rig is an asset to maintain and a resource to allocate, and they are the same object seen from two sides** — resources owns the calendar and maintenance owns the condition, so an asset out of service makes its resource unbookable through one link rather than two models of availability. **Retirement is not deletion**: a work order from three years ago still names the asset.

entries.what: Nothing on leave, overtime, minimum staffing levels, working-hour compliance or labour cost.
entries.why: The search returned nothing anywhere for labour cost, minimum staffing, working-hour limits, rest periods or union rules. 1.2.83 is labour-law compliance in the UAE and Oman, which is a legal obligation rather than a feature, and labour costing may belong in `finance`. **Unblocked 18 August** — held on CF-125, now closed. **A blocker that outlives its conflict is the backlog decaying in the way this apparatus exists to prevent**, and this is the second time in one day it happened. **Lane changed to deferred 18 August** — the decision behind it was taken (CF-134, CF-131, CF-125) and what remains is build, not a conversation.
entries.closedBy: RotaAssignment overtimeMinutes, restPeriodBefore, breachesWorkingHourLimit and labourCost. **UAE labour law limits hours and mandates rest and nothing counted either.** **Flagged at assignment, not at payroll** — finding out a month later means it was worked. And **a manager building a rota without seeing its cost finds out from finance.**

entries.what: No session participant manifest — who is in a session, in what order, with what package, and reordered by an operator mid-session.
entries.why: Distinct from duration, which variants already handle. A session holding a mix of first-time and experienced participants needs a running order because the order is operational — 1.3.44 balances the session by package. Overlaps CF-125's resource calendar, since an instructor is a resource assigned to the same session.
entries.fix: Model the session participant list once the resource decision lands.
entries.blockedNote: CF-125 — the resource and staff assignment model
entries.closedBy: getSessionManifest and reorderSessionManifest. **The running order is operational** — an instructor takes beginners first, and a manifest sorted by booking time puts one between two advanced riders.

entries.what: Deliberate oversell is not modelled.
entries.why: An envelope may be raised freely and reducing it below what has sold is refused, so the guard exists in one direction only. Free events oversell on purpose because no-show rates are known. Whether oversell is an envelope property or an admission policy is the design question.
entries.fix: Decide where an oversell allowance lives and how the gate behaves when capacity is exceeded.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. 1.4 closed without an oversell allowance appearing.
entries.closedBy: Envelope.oversellAllowance and oversellBasis. **The guard existed in one direction only.** An allowance on the envelope rather than an admission policy, because **the gate must still refuse at actual capacity** — overselling is a sales decision and admission is a safety one, and they must not share a number.

entries.what: No event template and no event duplication.
entries.why: `cloneSeatMap` clones a map and is the only clone in the package. An event carries schedules, ticket configuration, seating, resources and pricing, and duplicating it is not the same operation. Related to BL-030, product versioning and clone, from 1.1 — probably one mechanism.
entries.fix: One clone mechanism covering products and events.
entries.blockedNote: Ready, and clusters with BL-030 and BL-058.
entries.closedBy: Covered by the product versioning mechanism — listProductVersions, restoreProductVersion and cloneProduct. **An event template is a clone with the schedule left off**, and the walk itself called this the fourth appearance of one mechanism.

entries.what: The approval chain and the occurrence lifecycle sit on different entities, so neither is complete.
entries.why: Corrected after the capability search was extended to `states/`. `states/performance.yaml` already models scheduled, onSale, soldOut, suspended, cancelled and completed properly — soldOut computed both ways because an operator who has to set it will forget. What the matrix asks for and nothing provides is **draft, pendingApproval and approved on an occurrence**: those live on `ProductLifecycleState`, which governs the product, not the night. An event whose performances need sign-off has nowhere to record it.
entries.fix: Decide whether approval belongs on the performance, the event, or neither.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. 7.4.45 restated the lifecycle and confirmed `suspended` is absent.
entries.closedBy: Performance.approvalRequestId and requiresApprovalToCancel. **The approval chain and the occurrence lifecycle sat on different entities** — states/performance.yaml models the lifecycle properly and nothing said which transition somebody signs. **Set on the transition, not the entity**: publishing is routine, cancelling a sold performance is the act somebody signs, and binding approval to the whole entity would require a signature to reschedule a wet Tuesday.

entries.what: No event budget, cost tracking or profitability analysis.
entries.why: `finance` has cost centres and the ledger, so the posting side exists. What is missing is a budget held against an event and actuals compared to it. Whether that is a finance concern or a catalogue one is the home question.
entries.fix: Model an event budget against existing cost centres.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. 5.7 walked without an event budget appearing — cost centres exist, budgets do not.
entries.closedBy: EventBudget. **Cost centres exist and an event is not one** — standing versus one-off. **Profitability is revenue minus committed cost, not paid cost**: an event three weeks out with 40,000 of purchase orders raised has spent it.

entries.what: No sponsor packages, sponsor entitlements, sponsorship inventory or sponsor reporting.
entries.why: Sponsorship inventory is sellable capacity of a different kind — logo placements, hospitality allocations, naming rights. It may be a product kind, or it may be closer to partner agreements in `subscription`. Nothing exists today.
entries.fix: Decide whether sponsorship is a product kind or an agreement.
entries.blockedNote: 22.x Marketing & CRM
entries.closedBy: PartnerAgreement.sponsorship with placements, exclusivity and hospitality allocation. **A sponsor buys a relationship for a season, not a ticket for a date** — modelled on the agreement rather than as a ProductKind, because duplicating the commercial terms onto a product means two places to disagree. **Exclusivity is the expensive word**: a second agreement breaching it is a legal problem rather than a scheduling one.

entries.what: A guest cannot hold a credit account with partial payment against future bookings.
entries.why: `orders.CreditPosition` carries creditLimit, used, available and paymentTermsDays and is B2B only. 1.3.51 puts a 25,000 AED limit on an individual who books ahead and must settle X days before. Extending B2B credit to guests is plausible; whether a venue wants guest credit exposure is commercial.
entries.fix: Decide whether guest credit is in scope, then extend or decline.
entries.blockedNote: 2.x Ticketing Sales, where B2B credit is walked
entries.closedBy: openGuestCreditAccount. **CreditPosition is B2B only** and 1.3.51 puts a limit on an individual. **A partner is a company with a contract; a guest is a person with a phone number**, so requiresApproval defaults true.

entries.what: No event-triggered messaging, and a waiver is not held against the guest record.
entries.why: `sendTransactionalMessage` sends; nothing fires it from an event before, during or after. And a waiver captured at sale does not persist to the guest so a returning participant signs again. Related to BL-003, tenant notification branding — likely one messaging pass.
entries.fix: Event triggers on the campaign engine, and a waiver on the guest record.
entries.blockedNote: 22.x Marketing & CRM
entries.closedBy: MessageTrigger — a platform event, a template and an offset. **Before, during and after a visit are one mechanism with a different sign on the offset.** Suppression and consent are checked at send, not on the trigger.

entries.what: Metrics named in reporting requirements that have no source in the schema.
entries.why: Nineteen metrics added to MetricSource as their upstream models landed — inventoryValuation from StockBatch, resaleVolume from ResaleListing, **salesByInstructor from resources.Resource, which the enum deliberately refused to name this morning because nothing produced it.** **BL-053 was always going to close this way**: not by changing reporting but by building the things it wanted to report on. 28 rows remain and each names a metric still without a source.
entries.fix: Each remaining metric needs its upstream model, not a reporting change: inventory valuation waits on BL-114, resale on BL-060, instructor attribution on the resource assignment now in `resources`. **Close this by closing those**, and add the metric to `MetricSource` as each lands.
entries.blockedNote: CF-125, and 8.x Unified Operations Dashboard where reporting is walked
entries.closedBy: SeededReport, getSupplierPerformance, DataSource extended to 34, GuestProfile.engagementScore and SegmentCriterion documented. **BL-053 always closed by building what reporting wanted to report on, not by changing reporting** — nineteen metrics landed earlier as their sources appeared, and the last twenty-six needed four things. **ReportDefinition.isSystem existed and nothing populated it**: twenty-eight requirements asked for dashboards over data already there, and the answer to every one was *the builder can do that*, which is true and is not a deliverable. **A venue opening on Monday wants the reports every venue runs.** Supplier performance was the one real gap — receipts recorded what arrived and nothing scored it, and **OTIF is the measure procurement uses because a delivery that is early and short is not a good delivery.** **And two of the twenty-six were documentation rather than contract**: SegmentCriterion.attribute is free-form, so wallet-balance and portfolio segments were always expressible and nobody had said so.

entries.what: A product cannot be published on a future date or retired automatically.
entries.why: Archiving already runs on a timer, so the scheduling machinery exists in this contract. `effectiveFrom` appears on tax codes, FX rates and white-label policies and not on products. A seasonal product still needs somebody awake at midnight.
entries.fix: Put an on-sale window on the product and drive the live transition from it.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. 2.1 closed and no channel-level on-sale window appeared.
entries.closedBy: `Product.onSaleFrom` and `onSaleTo`. Archiving already ran on a timer in this contract, so the machinery existed.

entries.what: No impact analysis before a product change, and no propagation of a change to already-sold tickets.
entries.why: **The package already knows how to do this and does it in four places** — `PerformanceCancellationResult`, `RecognitionRunResult`, `FxRevaluationResult` and `PeriodCloseResult` all carry `dryRun` with an impact count. All four are expensive-and-irreversible operations. Changing a live product's price or entitlement is in the same category and has no dry run. 1.4.4 is the harder half: whether a change propagates to sold tickets is a commercial and legal question, not only a technical one.
entries.fix: A dry-run impact result on product change, and a stated propagation policy.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. 2.12 confirmed it — modifyOrder and exchangeOrderLines have no dry run while cancelPerformance does.
entries.closedBy: assessProductChange, modelled on PerformanceCancellationResult. Returns entitlements issued, orders affected, future performances and **open carts — a guest holding this product while its price changes underneath them**.  answers the second half: a name correction should, a price change must not.

entries.what: `Product` records no owner, creator, approver or responsible department.
entries.why: `SeatBlock` carries `createdByPrincipalId`, `Grant` carries it, `ManualDiscountRequest` carries `approverPrincipalId`. The precedent is in the package three times over and the product — which passes through an approval gate guarded on the approver not being the author — records neither party.
entries.fix: Add createdByPrincipalId, approvedByPrincipalId and a responsible department to Product, following the SeatBlock and ManualDiscountRequest precedent.
entries.closedBy: `Product.createdByPrincipalId`, `approvedByPrincipalId` and `responsibleDepartmentId` added, following the `SeatBlock` precedent.

entries.what: No bulk product upload, and no import or export of a catalogue between environments.
entries.why: `seating` has a two-phase import — parse to a preview with findings, then commit — built for exactly this shape of problem and validated against real client files. `catalogue` has nothing, so a venue with three thousand products creates them one at a time. Environment-to-environment export may belong with `platform-ops`, which already promotes releases dev to staging to production.
entries.fix: A catalogue import following the seating two-phase pattern.
entries.blockedNote: 2.x Ticketing Sales, to see whether pricing and channel data import with the product
entries.closedBy: importProductCatalogue and commitCatalogueImport, two-phase after seating.ImportJob. **replaceCategory is named so it can be refused** — replacing a category with live orders is a migration, not an import.

entries.what: No product version history, no restore, and no duplication.
entries.why: **Fourth appearance of one mechanism** — BL-030 product versioning at 1.1, BL-047 event templates at 1.3, and now version-restore and duplication here. `white-label` already implements the whole pattern for tenant configuration: `listConfigVersions`, `restoreConfigVersion`, `diffConfigVersion`, with a content hash. A product carries pricing, rules, entitlements and capacities and has none of it. This is one versioned-entity primitive resolving four entries, not four jobs.
entries.fix: A versioned-entity mechanism following the white-label ConfigVersion precedent, applied to products and events.
entries.blockedNote: Held for reconciliation clustering with BL-030 and BL-047 — one versioned-entity mechanism, not three jobs.
entries.closedBy: ProductVersion, following white-label.ConfigVersion. **A restore creates a new version rather than rewinding** — a price that was wrong for three days stays reproducible.

entries.what: Transaction rules are not per-product. A ticket type cannot state its own refund, exchange or transfer eligibility.
entries.why: `AdmissionProfile` covers usage rules well — validation window, max duration, re-entry limits, permitted access points. `getRefundPolicy` and `setRefundPolicy` are venue-scoped. A non-refundable promotional ticket and a flexible full-price ticket sold at the same venue cannot differ.
entries.fix: Attach a transaction-rule set to the product or the entitlement template.
entries.blockedNote: Ready, and larger than first written. 2.12.4 and 2.12.12 both make refund and exchange eligibility configurable by ticket status and access level, and getRefundPolicy remains venue-scoped.
entries.closedBy: AdmissionProfile.perProductRules. **Rules were per profile and a ticket type could not state its own**, so an annual pass allowing one entry per day and a single ticket allowing one entry ever needed two profiles. minimumGapMinutes rather than a boolean: **a guest returning from lunch in forty minutes is normal, and the same scan twice in ten seconds is a card passed back over a fence.**

entries.what: No resale listing entity, and a cart line cannot point at one.
entries.why: **Smaller than it first looked.** The original reading called this a missing bounded context and marked fifteen of nineteen rows as gaps; on checking, most ride machinery that already exists and is generic. `approvals` is generic over its subject — `CreateApprovalRequest` carries `subjectContract`, `subjectType` and `subjectId`, and automatic, manual and multi-level are `ApprovalMode` with levels, so 1.6.4 is an enum value rather than a workflow. Notifications, reporting, audit and APIs are all generic. `transferOrderTickets` already moves ownership on claim, credential reissue-and-blacklist is stated in `F23`, anti-passback sits on the access point and `getAvailability` validates capacity. **What is genuinely absent is one entity and one line kind**: a listing with a seller, an asking price and a lifecycle, and a `CartLine` that points at a listing rather than at `variantId`. Plus price-cap configuration and a fee definition, both small. **Note for the price caps: anti-scalping limits are regulated in several jurisdictions and whether that binds in the UAE and Oman should be checked before they are designed** — a research item, not a conflict.
entries.fix: A listing entity with a lifecycle, a cart line kind that references it, price-bound configuration and a resale fee.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. 2.12 settled the line question — `Order.payments` is a list and `CartLine` binds to `variantId`, so a listing needs its own line kind rather than a variant. `exchangeOrderLines` and `transferOrderTickets` give the lineage a resale would reuse.
entries.closedBy: ResaleListing. **Smaller than it first looked** — transfer, order and payment machinery all existed. **A resale is a transfer with money attached and the venue stays in the middle**: the seller entitlement is voided and a new one issued, so the ticket that admits is always one the venue issued, which is what stops a screenshot at the gate. **The seller is paid after the buyer is admitted**, because a resale refunded at the gate cannot be clawed back from a seller already paid.

entries.what: Cashier input mode, guest-facing display content and a web-like POS journey are stated nowhere.
entries.why: `Workstation` carries devices and a sale board, so the binding exists. What is missing is what the second screen shows — cart, price, offers, upsell — and whether the till is touch, keyboard or both. These read as screen concerns, and the package has no artefact class for POS presentation.
entries.fix: Decide whether guest-display content is configuration or screen specification.
entries.blockedNote: Device Management is walked at domain 16 and may own the display binding.
entries.closedBy: ConfigureWorkstationRequest cashierInputMode and guestDisplayContent. **A till operator who touch-types is slower on a touchscreen and a new starter is faster**, so the mode is per workstation because the operator is. **A second screen showing nothing is one the guest ignores when it does show something.**

entries.what: No configurable demographic or survey capture at the point of sale.
entries.why: Nationality, residency and guest type captured at the till is not feedback — `submitReview` is post-visit sentiment and a different thing entirely. **This is very likely the mechanism CF-69 is missing**: DET and DCT are the Dubai and Abu Dhabi tourism authorities, their reporting is fed from exactly this data, and CF-69 records that both are almost certainly mandatory and have no trace in any contract. If so this is a compliance obligation rather than a feature. **Unblocked 18 August** — held on CF-69, now closed.
entries.fix: Model configurable capture fields on the order, and confirm against the DET and DCT reporting schema.
entries.closedBy: FormDefinition of kind dataCapture at the point of sale, with isPersonalData marked per field. **Retention is decided at the field** — a survey answer and a medical condition on one form have different lifetimes.

entries.what: Nothing awards loyalty points when a ticketing order completes.
entries.why: A cashier can read a balance through `getLoyaltyPosition`, and `adjustLoyaltyPoints` is staff-only under `LEDGER_POST` — a manual correction, not an accrual. **`games` awards points on play and ticketing does not**, so a guest earns for an arcade game and not for a ticket. Pairs with BL-018, where a guest can see points and cannot spend them: the loyalty loop is closed at neither end.
entries.fix: An accrual on order completion, and a redemption path.
entries.blockedNote: Loyalty programmes are walked at 22.6 Gamification & Loyalty.
entries.closedBy: accrueLoyaltyPoints, fired by order completion and idempotent on the order. **games awarded points on play and ticketing did not**, so a guest earned for an arcade game and not for the ticket that got them in.

entries.what: No single guest-identification operation across QR, RFID, NFC, membership card, wallet, app, phone and email.
entries.why: `searchGuests` finds by name and contact; `lookupTicket` resolves a ticket. A cashier presented with a wristband has to know which operation to call. This is a resolver over identifiers rather than new data.
entries.fix: One identify operation taking a token of any kind and returning the guest with their entitlements, wallet and loyalty position.
entries.blockedNote: **Settled by the client at the 18 August F&B, Retail, Procurement & Inventory workshop.** **Decision: *a single, unified customer profile will be used across ticketing, F&B and retail to give a 360-degree view of guest activity and avoid duplicate records*.** Six appearances in the walk and now a client decision.
entries.closedBy: identifyGuest — one resolver over QR, RFID, NFC, membership card, wallet pass, phone, email, app device and plate. **Ambiguity is returned, not resolved**: two guests sharing a phone number is real, and picking one silently lands a sale on the wrong account.

entries.what: POS and kiosk accessibility — large text, high contrast, simplified navigation — is stated nowhere.
entries.why: Multilingual is contracted through `setLanguages`. Accessibility is one of the fifteen artefact classes and is closed, but it was closed against guest surfaces. **A kiosk in an entrance hall is the surface where accessibility matters most and the one with no accessibility statement.**
entries.fix: State accessibility behaviour for kiosk and POS surfaces.
entries.closedBy: AccessibilitySettings on TenantConfig. **A kiosk is the hard case** — a guest with low vision using a website brings their own assistive technology; at a kiosk they get whatever the kiosk offers. reachableHeightMode and sessionTimeoutMultiplier: **timeouts are an accessibility barrier nobody counts.**

entries.what: A kiosk cannot sell food or merchandise, though every operation it would need exists.
entries.why: `getGuestMenu`, `createGuestFnbOrder`, `listMerchandise` and `reserveMerchandise` are all contracted and guest-callable. **P05 has fifteen screens and none of them sells either** — KSK-003 asks what you are buying and calls `listProducts` alone. This is a screen gap against a complete contract, which is the opposite of every other gap found so far and cheaper to close.
entries.fix: Add F&B and merchandise paths to P05.
entries.blockedNote: Walked at 4.6 F&B POS ordering and 6.1 Retail.
entries.closedBy: KSK-016 Order Food and KSK-017 Shop. **Every operation existed and no screen called them** — getGuestMenu, createGuestFnbOrder, listMerchandise and reserveMerchandise are all contracted and guest-callable, and P05 had fifteen screens selling neither. **Allergens on the card, not behind a tap**: a guest at a kiosk with a queue behind them is not reading descriptions.

entries.what: No named reseller or channel-manager adapters.
entries.why: The commercial model is complete — `PartnerAgreement` carries net rates, commission, credit terms, products and channels; `alternative-codes` maps a partner SKU so an inbound order matches; F03 is the booking flow and P10 the portal. **What is missing is the integrations themselves**, and 2.1.5 says the provider lists which resellers it works with, which is a commitment nobody has made. CF-69 already holds four named integrations with no trace in any contract. **Unblocked 18 August** — held on CF-69, now closed.
entries.fix: Agree the reseller list, then build adapters against the existing agreement model.
entries.closedBy: ChannelListing.adapter with octoStandard named first. **The commercial model was complete and the wire was not.** OCTo is the standard the OTAs converged on, and **a per-OTA adapter is a per-OTA maintenance commitment** — naming the standard first is what keeps that list from growing.

entries.what: Checkout recommendation is rule-based; profile-and-cart-driven recommendation is parked.
entries.why: `getUpsellSuggestions` and `createUpsellRule` exist and work off configured rules. **The requirement is closer to built than CF-73 implies** — a rule-driven upsell at checkout satisfies most of 2.1.22 without a trained model, and only the profile-similarity half needs history. Worth revisiting what CF-73 parked. **Unblocked 18 August** — it was held on CF-73, which closed. A blocker that outlives its conflict is the backlog decaying in the way this apparatus exists to prevent.
entries.fix: Confirm how much of 2.1.22 the rule engine already satisfies, and park only the remainder.
entries.closedBy: getRecommendations with profile and cart input. **Deterministic fallback always** — a recommender returning nothing when the model is unavailable is a checkout with a hole in it. **Never recommends what is already in the cart, out of stock, or ineligible**: three checks that sound obvious and are the three most common defects in shipped recommenders.

entries.what: A distinct webstore API surface per venue is not stated.
entries.why: Multi-tenancy is per tenant with venue scoping on every operation, which serves a venue correctly without giving it its own surface. 2.6.6 may be asking for isolation we already provide by another means, or for a genuinely separate endpoint per venue. The requirement is one line and does not say which.
entries.fix: Confirm with the client whether per-venue means scoped or separate.
entries.closedBy: ApiClient.allowedTenantIds — 13.1.46. **A developer integrating for one venue must not reach another, and a client with an empty list reaches none.**

entries.what: No presentment currency — a storefront cannot show prices in a guest's currency.
entries.why: **CF-118 swept multi-currency and closed on the settlement half.** `FxRate` carries `purpose` and rates are configured rather than fetched live, with the reasoning that a market rate moving mid-shift means two guests pay different dirham amounts for the same ticket. That reasoning applies harder to a storefront: a displayed price that moves between browsing and checkout is a complaint. What is missing is a display rate distinct from the settlement rate, and a statement of which one binds at checkout.
entries.fix: A presentment rate with a stated binding point.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. 5.x walked — FxRate covers settlement; presentment currency did not appear.
entries.closedBy: PaymentProvider.presentmentCurrencies — what a storefront may quote in, distinct from what it settles in. **A guest sees GBP and the venue books AED.**

entries.what: No AI first-pass translation with human editing.
entries.why: `setLanguages` carries enabled languages, default, RTL and `translationGaps` reporting content missing a version — so the gap is already measured. What 2.6.34 adds is filling it automatically and letting a back-office user correct the result. Adjacent to `generateConfiguration`, which is built. **Unblocked 18 August** — it was held on CF-73, which closed. A blocker that outlives its conflict is the backlog decaying in the way this apparatus exists to prevent.
entries.fix: Translate into the gap, and keep the human edit.
entries.closedBy: ai.proposeTranslations. **setLanguages already measured the gap** and nothing filled it. **A first pass, never a publish** — a tenant own words in a language nobody at the venue reads is exactly the content that must not go live unreviewed. glossaryRef exists because without one **Ladies Night becomes a literal translation somebody has to find and undo.**

entries.what: No payment link. A booking taken at POS cannot be paid later by the guest.
entries.why: `paymentLink` exists as an attachment *kind* on a conversation message, so the delivery channel anticipated it and nothing generates one. This matters beyond convenience — a reservation held without payment is capacity nobody can sell, and the alternative is a call.
entries.fix: Generate a payment link against an order, with an expiry and a single-use guarantee.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. Third appearance — 2.6.38, 2.8.8, 2.12.28.
entries.closedBy: createPaymentLink with an expiry that **releases the hold, not just the link** — unpaid inventory nobody can sell is the failure this avoids.

entries.what: No cookie consent management — banner, categorisation, scanning, script blocking, multi-domain preference sharing or consent analytics.
entries.why: **`marketing-crm` holds a genuinely good PDPL consent register** — `ConsentPurpose` of marketing, personalisation, profiling, thirdPartySharing, aiProcessing and transactional, with `noticeVersion`, `expiresAfterMonths`, `isRequiredForService`, source per channel and full history. **It is a different obligation.** Publishing a cookie policy is text and `PolicyKind.cookie` already allows it; blocking an analytics script before consent is enforcement in the browser. 2.6.60 names GDPR, ePrivacy, CCPA, CPRA, LGPD and PDPL, so this is regulatory. **Normally bought rather than built** — cookie scanning means maintaining a cookie database, which is what OneTrust and Cookiebot exist to do.

entries.what: Payment is contracted; no payment provider is.
entries.why: The integration register already flags Stripe amber — *payment exists; the provider does not* — and NI Payment Gateway red. **Network International is the dominant UAE acquirer**, so a red there is not a small omission. Pairs with BL-004, tenant payment-provider configuration, found at 19.1. **Unblocked 18 August** — held on CF-69, now closed.
entries.fix: Model provider configuration beside settlement.
entries.closedBy: PaymentProvider with Network International and Stripe (CF-131, decided by Chinmay 18 August). **Two gateways is the number that forces an abstraction** — one can be hard-coded and two cannot.

entries.what: A partner is a flat account. No sub-users, no hierarchy, no partner-managed access controls.
entries.why: `registerPartner` creates a partner and nothing creates a user beneath one. 2.7.51 asks for Master Agency, Branch, Department and User with permissions, quotas, credit limits and pricing cascading down. **`tenancy` already has a scope tree with nearest-ancestor resolution (ADR-0018)** — the mechanism exists and is pointed at venues rather than partners. The requirement gives its own reason for sub-users: avoiding shared credentials, which is a security position rather than a convenience.
entries.fix: Decide whether the partner hierarchy reuses the tenancy scope tree or is its own.
entries.closedBy: PartnerUser on a branch scope path. **The answer was already in the package** — 2.7.51 asks for Master Agency, Branch, Department and User, which is a scope tree, and tenancy has one. Quota and credit resolve nearest-ancestor-wins like configuration, and **canManageUsers exists because a venue administering every travel agent staff list is a venue doing the agency HR.**

entries.what: No OTA channel manager, and therefore no marketplace price, inventory or guest-data exchange.
entries.why: **The integration register marks *Resellers & OTA* as covered against `orders` and `subscription`.** That is true of the commercial model — agreements, allocations, credit — and not of the integration. Viator, Klook, Headout and GetYourGuide are named at 2.7.53 and appear nowhere. A channel manager is a live two-way feed of availability and price with rate-limit and mapping concerns, not a portal. **Unblocked 18 August** — held on CF-128, now closed. **A blocker that outlives its conflict is the backlog decaying in the way this apparatus exists to prevent**, and this is the second time in one day it happened.
entries.fix: Decide build versus a channel-manager aggregator.
entries.closedBy: ChannelListing. **The integration register marked Resellers and OTA as covered, and that was true of the commercial model and not of the integration.** An OTA pulls a feed, caches it and sells against the cache — **so the gap between pushes is the oversell window**, and allocationUnits bounds it. guestDataScope states what comes back, because a ticket arriving with no contact detail cannot be reissued and the venue should know at listing time rather than at the gate.

entries.what: No ERP interface for partner invoicing and reconciliation.
entries.why: `subscription.generateInvoice` bills a tenant for their subscription — a different ledger from invoicing a partner for tickets sold. SAP is named at 2.7.41 and again at 5.12.7, and `finance` already has the ledger, legal entities and settlement machinery an export would draw on. **Unblocked 18 August** — held on CF-128, now closed. **A blocker that outlives its conflict is the backlog decaying in the way this apparatus exists to prevent**, and this is the second time in one day it happened.
entries.fix: An export and reconciliation interface against the existing ledger.
entries.closedBy: exportPartnerInvoice. **generateInvoice bills a tenant for the platform — a different ledger from invoicing a partner for tickets sold.** The export is a format, not an integration: finance already has the ledger and the legal entities. **Idempotent on the period**, because a month exported twice creates a duplicate liability in somebody else system.

entries.what: No partner-scoped branding. Co-branded logos on tickets and emails, and a partner storefront, have no trace.
entries.why: White-label is tenant-scoped throughout — `TenantConfig`, `BrandIdentity`, `setTheme`. A reseller selling a venue's tickets under their own brand is a second scope level the model does not have. Adjacent to BL-002, the missing footer, in that both are white-label surface questions.
entries.fix: Decide whether partner branding is a scope on tenant config or a separate profile.
entries.closedBy: PartnerAgreement.brandingAssetId and storefrontSubdomain. **Co-branding rather than replacement** — the venue identity stays on the ticket because the ticket admits to the venue.

entries.what: No electronic acceptance, digital signature or acceptance version history on a partner agreement.
entries.why: `PartnerAgreement` carries `version` and `status`, so versioning exists; what is missing is the partner's act of accepting a version and the evidence of it. `signatureRef` already exists on inspections and approval decisions, so the primitive is in the package.
entries.fix: Record partner acceptance against an agreement version, following the signatureRef precedent.
entries.closedBy: PartnerAgreement acceptedByPrincipalId, acceptedVersion and signatureRef. **An agreement accepted with no version recorded is one nobody can produce in a dispute.**

entries.what: No partner API credential lifecycle — request, generate, rotate, revoke, scope.
entries.why: `SsoProviderConfig.clientSecretRef` is inbound SSO for staff. A partner calling our API needs outbound credentials scoped to their agreement's products and channels, and rotation is the part that matters — a key that cannot be rotated is a key that never is. **Domain 13 Developer & API Management is one of the three uncontracted domains (CF-21)** and is where this probably belongs.
entries.fix: Model partner credentials with the developer portal.
entries.closedBy: ApiClient with rotate and revoke. **Rotation without an overlap is an outage**; revocation has none by definition, and active tokens die with it.

entries.what: Partner pricing has no volume threshold, seasonality or segment tier.
entries.why: Price lists per channel and `netRates` on the agreement cover flat partner pricing. A tier that changes at a volume threshold needs the sale to look back at cumulative volume, which nothing does.
entries.fix: Extend price resolution with tier conditions.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. 2.9 and 2.14 both confirmed — no volume, seasonality, tier or residency pricing.
entries.closedBy: PartnerAgreement.volumeTiers, volumeWindow and seasonalRates. **The window is the argument, not the tier**: a partner selling 400 in January and 400 in February is either a 400-tier partner twice or an 800-tier partner once, and the two are different money. appliesRetrospectively is stated because **retrospective is what a partner assumes and prospective is what a venue budgets for.**

entries.what: No call disposition and no callback or follow-up activity.
entries.why: A conversation can be closed; nothing records why it ended — information, no sale, sale successful — which is the measure a contact centre runs on. And an agent cannot schedule a callback with a time, reason and assignee. `Case` is the nearest thing and a case is measured in hours where a callback is a diary entry.
entries.fix: Disposition on conversation close, and a follow-up activity.
entries.closedBy: CallDisposition with nine outcomes and a scheduled callback. **A conversation could be closed and nothing recorded why**, so every one looked identical in a report — and a promise to ring back lived in somebody notebook.

entries.what: No telephony integration — no screen pop, call control, recording or agent state from a phone system.
entries.why: `ConversationChannel` includes `voice` **with nothing behind it**, so the conversation model anticipated telephony and stops at the enum. Genesys, Avaya, Amazon Connect, Microsoft Teams and 3CX are named at 2.8.11 and none is in the integration register. CF-99 built agent state, queue and handover for chat — the same machinery serves voice if something feeds it. **Unblocked 18 August** — held on CF-128, now closed. **A blocker that outlives its conflict is the backlog decaying in the way this apparatus exists to prevent**, and this is the second time in one day it happened.
entries.fix: Decide the telephony platform, then adapt the existing conversation queue.
entries.closedBy: Conversation.telephony. **ConversationChannel included voice with nothing behind it** — the model anticipated telephony and stopped at the enum. **Not an integration, a binding**: the providers do call control themselves, and what the platform needs is the call bound to the guest and the case so an agent who answers already knows who is calling. **A recording reference with no consent record is a recording nobody may play.**

entries.what: No zero-value reissue of an expired entitlement for a later date.
entries.why: `rescheduleOrder` moves a live entitlement. An expired one — the guest missed the slot — has no path, and the requirement is explicit that this is a zero-value goodwill act rather than a sale. The precedent is in the same contract: `reprintOrder` reissues media and `exchangeOrderLines` swaps entitlements, both preserving lineage.
entries.fix: A zero-value reissue on an expired entitlement, under permission and audited.
entries.closedBy: reissueEntitlement — zero-value, with a closed reason set. **A goodwill act with no money in it**, and treating it as a refund plus a sale puts two transactions through the ledger for a gesture that moved nothing. **A reissue with no audit is indistinguishable from a ticket appearing from nowhere.**

entries.what: An operator cannot enter an arbitrary price, only an approved discount.
entries.why: `applyManualDiscount` takes an amount or percentage with a reason code and an approver. Setting a price outright is a different control — a discount is bounded by the list price and an override is not — and `PriceVariance` already exists in `finance` for exactly this kind of exception, reviewed after the fact.
entries.fix: Decide whether price override is a discount with no ceiling or its own operation posting a variance.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. 2.13 walked without at-gate price override appearing.
entries.closedBy: OrderLine.overridePrice with a closed reason set and escalation above a threshold. **A price match against a competitor is not a discount off a list — it is a number somebody decided.** A free-text override reason is an override nobody can report on, and this is the field an auditor reads first.

entries.what: A refund cannot settle into an advance balance or by wire transfer.
entries.why: `alternateTender` covers switching the method of a till refund. Refunding a settled B2B transaction into the partner's credit balance, or paying it out by wire, is a settlement act rather than a till act — and `CreditPosition` and `finance`'s settlement machinery both exist to receive it.
entries.fix: Refund destinations beyond tender: credit balance and bank settlement.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. 5.7 confirmed — refund settles by tender only; no credit-balance or wire destination.
entries.closedBy: Refund.settleTo — original tender, advance balance, wire or store credit. **originalTender stays the default because refunding elsewhere is how money laundering works**, and anything else needs a reason.

entries.what: Which exchange rate a cross-currency refund uses is unstated.
entries.why: `Payment` records `tenderCurrency`, `fxRate` and `fxRateSource` at the moment of sale, so the sale rate is retrievable. **CF-118 settled the principle that a rate moving between two guests is unacceptable and did not settle this case** — refunding at today's rate repays a different amount than was paid, and refunding at the sale rate exposes the venue to the movement. It is a commercial choice, and `PartnerAgreement.fxPolicy` already models exactly this choice for partners with `rateAtSale`, `rateAtInvoice` and `fixedRate`. **Unblocked 18 August** — it was held on CF-118, which closed. A blocker that outlives its conflict is the backlog decaying in the way this apparatus exists to prevent.
entries.fix: State the refund rate policy, reusing the fxPolicy vocabulary.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. 5.7 walked without a cross-currency refund rate policy appearing.
entries.closedBy: Refund.fxRate and fxVariance — **the rate on the original payment, not today's**. A guest who paid 100 USD at 3.67 and is refunded at 3.72 gets back more AED than they gave. The exposure runs both ways and neither is defensible, because **the guest did nothing but wait.** The difference books as an FX variance rather than hiding in the refund.

entries.what: Nothing states that a refund reverses the tax entry it created.
entries.why: `reverseJournalEntry` exists and `calculateTax` exists, so both halves are present and the obligation is implied rather than contracted. **An implied tax reversal is the kind of thing that is correct in the first implementation and wrong in the second**, and `finance` is an append-only ledger where a correction is an entry — the pattern is already established.
entries.fix: State tax reversal on the refund operation and in the posting rules.
entries.closedBy: Refund.taxReversalEntryId. Both halves existed and the obligation was implied — **an implied obligation is one a developer can miss without failing anything.**

entries.what: An order cannot be split into independent orders, nor several merged into one.
entries.why: Both requirements insist financial traceability survives, which is the hard part and which the append-only ledger makes tractable — a split is two new orders each carrying a link to the original, not an edit. Group bookings are the driver: a coach party that splits payment, or several reservations consolidated for one invoice.
entries.fix: Split and merge as lineage-preserving operations.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. 2.13 and 2.14 both walked; group and family handling is BL-013 and split/merge remains absent.
entries.closedBy: splitOrder. **A group that booked together and now pays separately.** Payments follow the lines they paid for — **a split leaving one payment against two orders is a reconciliation nobody can do**, so a partly-paid order refuses until the payment is allocated.

entries.what: No bulk price change across a category or globally.
entries.why: `BulkUpdateSeatsRequest` is the only bulk operation anywhere in 778 operations, and it takes a selection plus the attribute to set — a usable precedent. Repricing every adult admission before a season is a routine act that currently loops one price at a time, and a loop that fails halfway leaves a price list half-changed.
entries.fix: A bulk price operation with a selection, following the seating precedent, and atomic application.
entries.blockedNote: Ready. 2.13 walked without a bulk price operation appearing.
entries.closedBy: bulkChangePrices, following BulkUpdateSeatsRequest — a selection plus an adjustment, dry run by default. ** is part of the act**: a 7% rise gives 53.61 and nobody prices a ticket at 53.61.

entries.what: No transaction or booking fee, and therefore no fee line to itemise at checkout.
entries.why: **The cleanest gap in domain 2** — four rows, one concept, no dependencies. `orders` already separates `serviceCharge` from a tip with the reasoning that *it is revenue in most jurisdictions*, so the distinction between a charge and a gratuity is understood; the fee itself is absent. A fee is a line with its own tax treatment and its own posting account, which `finance` account mappings already handle for every other posting event type.
entries.fix: A fee definition by channel and product, fixed or percentage, resolved onto the order as its own line with a posting account.
entries.closedBy: OrderLine.feeKind. **A fee is a line, not an adjustment** — a guest is entitled to see what they are being charged for, and a fee folded into the ticket price is one nobody can question. A cancellation fee is usually the one thing not refunded, which only works if it is its own line.

entries.what: Pro-rata upgrade pricing is not computed.
